chapter: Touring, band and money in the 1950s-60s
title: Leaving Chess and recording best work for Imperial
summary: Contracts lapsed when sales faded; he made many records for Imperial which he considers his best.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Why did you split with Ches?

Well, there's all record companies. If you make so many records and they don't seem to be selling too good, well, the contract is no longer good. So this is what happened. I made quite a few records for Imperial. I think Luke Sheldon. Yeah, he was the owner. Yeah. They produced all of them. Yeah. I think I recorded my best. You got a bottle.

I did my best recordings on Imperial. To me, you know, what I consider the best. I was older. I was not an old man who had been in a wheelchair, but I was older and I had learned a whole lot. I had been out there playing music and whatnot. And, well, like I said, experienced.
You were only about 21, 22 years old.
Yeah, but I had been out there for a good while then. Even at 21 and 22, I was a veteran in the business.
